question: Which of the following states showed highest levels of poverty, in the 2011 census?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has consistently been one of the states with the highest levels of poverty in India.
 
• According to the 2011 Census, Bihar had a very high percentage of its population living below the poverty line.
 
• The lack of industrial development and high population density contribute to the high poverty rates in Bihar.
 
• Efforts have been made to improve the situation, but challenges remain due to infrastructural and socio-economic factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Poverty**

 
 
• Poverty is a state where an individual or community lacks the financial resources and essentials for a minimum standard of living.
 
• It is a multifaceted concept that includes social, economic, and political elements.
 
• In India, poverty is often measured using income levels and consumption patterns.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Line in India**
 
 
• The poverty line is an economic benchmark used to measure the minimum level of income required to secure the necessities of life.
 
• In India, the poverty line is determined by the Planning Commission based on the expenditure required for a minimum calorific intake and other basic needs.
 
• As per the Tendulkar Committee report, the poverty line is based on consumption expenditure and includes spending on food, education, health, etc.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census**
 
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census since 1871 and was conducted by the Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The census collected data on various socio-economic parameters including population, poverty levels, literacy rates, housing conditions, and employment.
 
• This data is crucial for policy-making and implementation of welfare schemes.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Alleviate Poverty**
 
 
• **MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act)**: Provides at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**: Aims to provide affordable housing to the urban poor with a target of building 20 million affordable houses by 31 March 2022.
 
• **National Food Security Act (NFSA)**: Aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's 1.2 billion people.
 
• Various state-specific initiatives and central schemes aim to target poverty reduction through skill development, financial inclusion, and social security measures.
